parole.significato: legion (military unit in the Roman army)
parole.testo: From Old Church Slavonic лег҄еонъ (legʹjeonŭ), borrowed from Byzantine Greek λεγιών (legiṓn). Ultimately from Latin legō (“to gather”) + -ион (-ion).
Inherited from Old Church Slavonic митрополиꙗ (mitropolija), from Byzantine Greek μητρόπολις (mētrópolis).
Inherited from Old Church Slavonic мощи pl (mošti), the plural of мощь (moštĭ, “power”). Probably a calque of Byzantine Greek δυνάμεις (dunámeis, “powers, manifestations of sainthood/divinity”).

parole.significato: stade (unit of length approximately equal to 180 m)
parole.testo: From Old Church Slavonic стадии (stadii, “stade”), borrowed from Byzantine Greek στάδιος (stádios, “measure of length”), a substantivation of Ancient Greek στάδιος (stádios, “firm, fixed”). Cognate with Latin stadium whence the recent doublet стадио́н (stadión, “stadium”).
